YOUR WORKING DIRECTORY IS `/opt/nxeon-agent-p1` (git worktree, branch agent/hosting-p1) of the Nxeon shared-hosting platform (Next.js 15 App Router + Tailwind + Prisma). Do ALL work there. NEVER touch /opt/nxeon (live prod) or other /opt/nxeon-* worktrees. `cd /opt/nxeon-agent-p1` first. node_modules symlinked; tsc/build work.

# MISSION: Phase 1 of a website-first restructure of shared hosting. Make it the cleanest, easiest way to run one site or ten — "simple by default, power on tap." You have latitude to improvise and improve.

## YOUR SPEC — read these two files in your worktree root FIRST
- `SCREENMAP_REFERENCE.html` — the COMPLETE numbered screen & section map (every page + sub-section). Build to this.
- `BLUEPRINT_REFERENCE.html` — the logic/data model + decisions (pooled plan, Website = atomic unit, flexible email pool, domains three ways).
Then DELETE both reference files before committing (they must not ship).

## DESIGN SYSTEM — NON-NEGOTIABLE (this is why past attempts were rejected as "AI slop")
- NO EMOJIS anywhere in the UI. Use `components/ui/Icon.tsx` (the inline-SVG `<Icon name=.. />` set — extend it if you need a glyph) and `components/ui/AppLogo.tsx` (real WordPress/app logos).
- Use the real design system, not invented CSS: `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (PageHeader, StatCard, StatusDot, Badge, EmptyState, fmtBytes, timeAgo) + the global `.card`/`.btn-primary`/`.btn-secondary`/`.btn-ghost`/`.btn-danger`/`.input`/`.label` utility classes. Fonts are Geist globally — don't set font-family; mono only for hostnames/paths.
- Match the house style of the existing panels; keep it calm and uncluttered.

## BUILD ON WHAT EXISTS — do not rebuild working panels
The current `components/customer/hosting/HostingConsole.tsx` already has a plan console + website drill-down + Icon + AppLogo + thumbnails + independent free-subdomain creation (`createFreeSubdomainSite`). EXPAND it to the full screen map. Reuse verbatim: `FileManager`, `DatabasesPanel`, `Backups`, `EmailTab`, `AppInstaller`, `CronPanel`, `PhpSwitcher`, `HostingUpgradePanel`, `AppCredentials`, `SubdomainsPanel`/`AddonDomainsPanel`. Read `lib/actions-hosting.ts` (toView/HostingAccountView, listWebsites, listHostingTaskLog, install/set-primary/delete, email-per-domain actions) + `lib/hosting-email.ts`.

## WHAT TO BUILD (Phase 1)
The model: HostingAccount = the Plan (capacity: sites, storage, mailbox pool, DBs). "Websites" (primary + addon/independent-subdomain + legacy subdomain) are first-class peers in the LOGIC + UI layer over the existing storage — NO physical DB migration of live data. Kill all "primary-domain-centric" framing.

1. **Plan console (screen map §2)** — clean, website-first. Header (plan name rename + tier + status + one Add-Website / Upgrade). Left section-nav scoping the plan: **Overview · Websites · Domains · Email · Databases · Backups · Activity · Settings**. Overview = resource cards (that nav) + website grid + recent activity + plan/usage. Cut all redundancy (single Add/Upgrade entries; one merged plan card).
2. **Website page (screen map §3)** — a self-contained per-site console with sub-nav **Overview · Site/App · Domain & SSL · Email · Backups** up front and an **Advanced** drawer folding **Files · Database · PHP · Cron · SSH/SFTP · Staging · logs**. NOTHING about "primary" bleeds in. Rich Overview (preview/thumbnail, app + admin login, stats, quick actions, recent activity). Reuse existing panels, scoped to the site.
3. **Flexible email pool (§2.4, the headline feature)** — the plan unlocks N mailboxes (from the plan's mailbox limit); the customer allocates them across ANY of their domains — pick the domain per mailbox, never all pinned to one. Show pool usage (X of N used across all domains). Build/adjust the actions so mailbox count is enforced against the pool across all domains, and adding a mailbox picks its domain. Reuse the per-domain email work already in `hosting-email.ts`/`EmailTab.tsx`; wrap it in a pool view.
4. **Domains page (§2.3)** — every domain in the plan + how attached: free subdomain / connected / registered; add via free-subdomain, connect-existing (DNS wizard), or buy (there's a Namecheap integration — surface "buy a domain" even if it links to the existing domain-search flow); assign a domain to a website; set a site's primary.
5. **Onboarding — Add-website wizard (§4)** — name → pick domain (free subdomain default / connect / buy) → what is it (WordPress recommended / blank+upload / app) → live + a friendly go-live checklist. Reuse `createFreeSubdomainSite` + install actions.
6. **Progressive disclosure everywhere** — simple surfaces by default; Advanced folded. This is the anti-clutter principle; honor it on every page.
7. Databases (§2.5), Backups (§2.6), Activity (§2.7), Settings (§2.8) — plan-scoped sections reusing existing panels.

Improvise/improve where it clearly helps (e.g. a nicer empty state, a smarter checklist, sensible defaults) — but stay on the design system and don't add scope creep (no page-builder, no migration UI, no AI, no white-label — those are later phases).

## HARD REQUIREMENTS
- Preserve EVERY existing feature + ownership/security guard; live hosting must keep working. Back-compat: existing accounts render correctly (their primary domain shows as their first website).
- Real data/actions only — no mock data.
- Delete the two reference HTML files before committing.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. After any schema/prisma change: `npx prisma generate` first (avoid schema changes if you can — this phase is logic+UI over existing storage).
- FULL build MUST pass (catches 'use server' + boundary errors tsc misses):
  `export $(grep -E '^DATABASE_URL=' /opt/nxeon-staging/.env | xargs) && npm run build` → "Compiled successfully" + all pages generated, exit 0. (A sync export in a 'use server' file fails the build — keep server actions async-only.)
- `npx tsx --test test/hosting.test.ts` → no NEW failures (pre-existing `fpm pool` failure is fine).
- Emoji scan your output (`grep -rP "[\x{1F000}-\x{1FAFF}]" components/customer/hosting`) and report it clean.

## DELIVERABLE
Commit to agent/hosting-p1 (clear message). Do NOT push/deploy. Report: the new page/route structure vs the screen map (what's built, what's deferred), the flexible email pool logic, how websites are now first-class (and primary-centrism removed), the onboarding wizard, which panels you reused, any improvements you improvised, confirmation tsc + full build + tests pass + emoji-clean, and every shared-file edit. Be explicit about anything from the screen map you did NOT get to so I can finish it.
